children: KANSAS CITY, Mo., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sunlife U.S. and the Kansas City Royals have completed another season of Royal Moves, a four-week wellness program designed to help kids embrace health and fitness. Combining baseball and softball fundamentals with everyday wellness lessons, the program aims to help build healthy habits that extend beyond the field and into kids' homes and communities.

Royal Moves had 360 student participants this year, from four Kansas City Public Schools elementary schools: George Washington Carver, George Melcher, Phillis Wheatley and Garfield. Following a program kickoff on September 25 at the Royals game against Cleveland, Royal Moves ran for four weeks, offering weekly fitness and health activities, and field trips to the Kansas City Urban Youth Academy.

"Helping kids discover the fun in being active is an important way to encourage healthy habits for life," said Ryan Bohrer, vice president of Commercial Dental and Vision, Sunlife U.S. "We love working with the Royals and connecting with the Kansas City community. Together, we're making health and wellness more approachable for those who need it most."

Weekly lessons pair wellness themes with baseball or softball skills: movement with base running and agility; nutrition and hydration with hitting; rest with throwing and caring for the body; and mindfulness with fielding, focus and self-control. Students complete mindfulness journal entries and track physical activity, water intake, food choices and sleep, with a goal of 60 active minutes daily.

"This program gives us a meaningful way to connect with students and show how small, everyday choices support their health and wellbeing," said Donease Smith, executive director, Kansas City Urban Youth Academy. "Royal Moves brings those lessons to life and helps families learn and grow together."

The program culminated on Saturday, October 24, with a Family Field Day at the Urban Youth Academy, bringing participating students, teachers, and families together for games and activities, including whiffle ball and a pumpkin patch. The event also featured a special book reading of 'Ruby Jean's Garden' by Chris Goode, founder of Ruby Jean's Juicery in Kansas City.

Sunlife has partnered with the Royals since 2017, supporting youth fitness, community health programs and local nonprofits. The partnership extends through the 2030 baseball season. This year, Sunlife and the Royals launched "Every Single Smile," with Sunlife donating $50 to TeamSmile for each Royals regular-season single. The campaign reached its $50,000 goal to help expand access to dental care for underserved Kansas City youth.
